statement: A garden is a rectangle 6 m long and 3 m wide. A fence goes all the way round it. How long is the fence?

choices.misconception: I added one long side and one short side and forgot the two sides opposite them.
I added the two long sides and forgot the two short sides.
I added three sides and missed the last short side.
I thought all four sides were 6 m long, as if the garden were a square.

hints: A rectangle has four sides. How long is each one?
Draw the rectangle and write a length on every side. Opposite sides of a rectangle are equal, so two sides are long and two are short. The fence is all four added together.
Two sides are 6 m and two sides are 3 m. Add 6 and 6, then add 3 and 3, then put the two answers together.

solutions.reliable: A rectangle has two long sides of 6 m and two short sides of 3 m. Going all the way round: 6 + 3 + 6 + 3 = 18, so the fence is 18 m long. The idea to keep: write a length on every side before you add, so no side is missed.
solutions.elegant: Going halfway round is one long side and one short side, 6 + 3 = 9 m. The whole way round is twice that, 18 m. The idea to keep: half the way round a rectangle is one length plus one width.

whyOnTest: Perimeter means every side, and the usual slip is adding only the two numbers printed in the question.
author: Devansh Sanghavi
